verdict.tagline: Strategic brilliance battles technical friction and punishing tactical RNG.
for_you_if: you love deep tactical turn-based combat
you enjoy demanding base management systems
you can plan around unpredictable chance rolls
not_for_you_if: you need stable performance on ultrawide monitors
you will not deal with third-party launchers
you want to avoid save file corruption

claims.claim: The user interface does not display correctly on aspect ratios above 16:9, making the game unplayable on ultrawide monitors without a fix.

citations.review_text: Game needs a patch to support modern resolutions. The UI does not display correctly on any aspect ratio above 16:9. Widely-known issue with no fix, whether it be through mods or INI edits.
Altough i like the gameplay elements, sadly the game is unplayable on Ultrawide monitors. Setting the game to a 16:9 aspect ratio is not an option for me personally. Beware.

claims.claim: Players experience softlocks and crashes during menus such as the promotion screen and loadout menu, forcing them to quit the game.

citations.review_text:
I didn't even make it to 2 hours before running into a parade of bugs:

Promotion screen after battle? Softlocked.
Loadout menu? Also broken and will softlock you as well.
The fix? By quitting the game, there's no other fix as far as I searched the internet.

Look, I expect XCOM to screw me over with impossible shots and bad RNG, that's part of the charm. But getting screwed over by basic functionality that should've been tested? That feels like a major oversight from the devs, and honestly? I'm not sticking around to see what breaks next.
buggy, got stuck twice with no other choice but to quit the game

claims.claim: The game features a third-party launcher that creates instability and requires manual workarounds to bypass.

citations.review_text:
This is your annual reminder that 2K and Firaxis felt like they needed to create <3 Launchers <3 for all their Games, that said Launchers are universally viewed as utter traaash, to the point it has been removed with great shame on Civ 5 & Civ 6, and they legit felt the need to say they wouldn't make launcher for Civ 7 as sale advertisement. 

But for some, like, reasons. It's still there to haunt you on Xcom and Xcom2 and create instability. For this Game, let's say that if you desire to launch it without the launcher, you have to hack the .exe, better hope you won't have problems with it.

Apparently, even games from 2012 that you played without difficulties can still be broken by some genius manager for no reasons at all.

Amazing devs why just spend 1 day to fix the game?

why is this game so popular when it's littered with game breaking bugs?

ironman is basically impossible because there are bugs that can and will brick your entire save such as soldiers getting stuck in the world or a bug that makes it so you can't switch soldiers

game also lacks extremely basic features such as move confirm. misclicks are permanent so don't expect to be able to multitask while "playing" this agonizingly slow game because if you click back into the game and accidentally move a solder then you just waste their life.

the developers are amateur

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the story is thin with a limited number of plot points and can feel repetitive by the end.

citations.review_text:
It’s a good game, and maybe within the context of its era it would even be considered a great game.  However, I was disappointed that the story was shallow and with a very limited number of plot points.  Aliens are attacking, go kick their butts, steal their technology, use it to fight new aliens…  It got repetitive by the end.

Now, the combat and strategy was well developed which is what really made the game.  The different classes and their unique unlockable abilities added a lot of depth, and motivated me to build an unstoppable team.  My only complaint about the combat was the multi-leveled maps the cursor would glitch between the levels depending on the camera angle and it was sometimes a struggle to get the soldier to the correct spot.

The base management helped to drive the story a bit, introduce extra strategy elements, and give a nice break between missions.  Although, it didn’t seem necessary to fully develop the base for balancing the funds between competing priorities was difficult.  I was always broke at first then all of a sudden towards the end of the game I had a glut of money when I learned to prioritize satellites.  The UFO interceptions didn’t seem as well developed as the rest of the game.

Overall: 7/10

I'll divide my review into each section of the game.

Early game: Can be absolutely miserable if you're going in blind. You'll breeze through the first few missions, then suddenly get hit with a more complex one that wipes your entire squad. That first major loss will likely spiral into a restart if you don't know what you're doing.

Mid game: This is where the game really shines. Your soldiers become much stronger, your base starts coming together, and the missions feel challenging without being unfair. It's easily the most enjoyable part of the game.

Late game: Mostly as good as the mid game, except for one section near the end where you have to shoot down a UFO to progress the story. This is probably the worst part of the game because the aircraft you need take around two weeks to build, and during that time the strategic layer can completely fall apart while you're forced to wait.

I'd still recommend the game. The story is a bit thin, but the gameplay is excellent. Just know that some of the design choices will punish you with zero remorse, and the game expects you to learn from your mistakes. That's just part of the experience.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that early mistakes in base management and resource allocation can ruin an entire campaign.

citations.review_text:
Enemy Unknown and Map Unseen

XCOM: Enemy Unknown is a highly renowned squad based tactical game mixed with base and resource management systems.  I completed this game without any mods or DLC, so this review is based on just the game as it is today.

As an additional caveat, I should mention that I've never played a game in this genre before, so I don't really have a baseline to judge the game on, just how I felt after completing the game.

It took me three different attempts from the very start of the game to manage to beat it.  My first attempt ended incredibly early on because I didn't have any real idea what I was doing.  My second attempt lasted longer, but when I realized I had missed some important aspects of base management, I was already in a death spiral.  My final attempt went much better and I ended the game only having lost 8 soldiers, but it required me to reload a few missions to prevent total failure.

I went into XCOM believing that it was the kind of game that wants you to push past failures since any single failure doesn't end your run.  This was a massive mistake.  The way that this game escalates in difficult makes it so that early mistakes can ruin your entire run.  There are several systems that, when you're doing well, give you massive rewards, but when you make a minor mistake, they can prevent you from making any real headway.  For example, you begin the game with a max squad size of 4 soldiers, but you can eventually increase that size to 6.  2 extra soldiers massivily increases your survivability, formation ability, and damage output, so it's one of the most important upgrades to get.  This upgrade is locked behind having soldiers that have ranked up a certain amount, so if you don't keep your soldiers alive for about a dozen missions, with them consistently earning kills, you'll never get to increase your squad size, and you'll constantly be on the back foot.

There are other mechanics that have similar cascading effects where…

Took me quite a while to finally getting around to playing XCOM, but I'm glad I did, as I had a pretty good time playing through it, even if it does have a few issues.

The story felt a lot like the plot of a B movie (which isn’t necessarily a bad thing). You're tasked with protecting the Earth from an alien invasion while trying to develop new technologies to fight against the alien's vastly superior technology and trying to understand what the aliens are after. It's definitely a bit shallow and predictable, but it still felt interesting enough to keep the experience enjoyable.

I played through the game on the easiest difficulty and it didn't propose much of a challenge in terms of gameplay, although I still enjoyed it. You manage a military base, making choices on what things to spend money on (research, weapons, facilities, soldiers, reconnaissance, etc.), which is interrupted whenever an alien attack occurs. When this happens, you fly your soldiers out to the site of the conflict and the game transitions into turn-based combat between you and the aliens. The management of your base feels quite daunting at first, as it's hard to tell what you should prioritize, and making the wrong decisions early can cost you later, but once you learn how everything works, it gets a lot easier. The combat felt pretty easy for the most part (likely due to the difficulty I chose), although there were a few things I still found frustrating, and made me glad I didn't try to beat the game on a harder difficulty:
[list]
[*] You typically only learn where the enemies are by moving your soldiers close enough to them, and the aliens only attack you once you've discovered them on the map. However, this means accidentally discovering an alien when performing your last move on the turn can be extremely punishing, and can feel a bit unfair.
[*] It isn't always clear how close you need to be to an alien to shoot them, or whether one position will provide a better shot than another. There wer…

claims.claim: Reviewers report that enemy pods trigger through fog of war and react immediately, making line-of-sight management essential to avoid being overwhelmed.

citations.review_text:
I'm coming at this from someone who played a couple hundred hours of X Com 2 first and X com 2 has basically everyone improvement this game needed. I think its still good game in general but I hate it. I did not expect this game to be such a rough work in every way but I applaud Firaxis for learning. I'd like to judge it in its right but its just pretty ♥♥♥♥ in its right for me. I'm used to getting my playthrough ended since that's XCOM BABY but not on a Council Mission where an alien turned a corner and started combat then killed 3/5 in that same instance.

It's buggy in different ways than it's sequel and entirely based cowardice.  You WILL get an enemy Overwatch from fog of war. You WILL inch ever so slightly forward where the enemy is visible and they turn to shoot because the game didn't notify you battle even started (I encountered a pod of Mutons very clearly just out of LoS. They didnt look to retreat, Overwatch, even shoot that turn. Notifying me that I believed I had caught them just out of their vision radius. They were still all facing each other in an idle animation. I end the turn. One of the Mutons turns around and pops a soldier dead.) You WILL get your "stealth" blown from areas it shouldn't have been, and get enemies in fog of war from behind a damn tree. You WILL waste time on meld because the best option in nigh every single situation is just inch forwards ever so slightly. 

It's not even as if  I would play chicken in X2 when the mission would allow you to. But it always felt more valuable or strategic waiting for the perfect setup to start an encounter. With no stealth in this game, the lacking skill trees feeling like there's little to no cohesive combos, and the allow penchant for fleeing or shooting on the spot, makes inching the only option for everything up until where im at at least.

Basically everything had a give and take in X com 2. Each monster added a problem to solve and a pattern or weakness to be abused. All the aliens up until …

The game is extremely buggy, it constantly freezes, crashes, or softlocks, and the gameplay is incredibly frustrating.

The challenge of XCOM is managing risk. Hedging your bets, and making sure the infamous "Missed 99% shot" doesn't result in a game over. In practice, this doesn't matter, because the REAL challenge is how well you can game the enemy "pod" activation. Enemies don't do anything until they enter your line of sight, so instead of trying to keep eyes on all the important chokepoints or get a clear view of things for your sniper, you want to instead make yourself as blind as humanly possible to mitigate the chance of activating multiple pods. If you get dogpiled, you are probably going to wipe. So gouge out your eyes and minimize the amount of map you can actually see.

The gameplay itself is also extremely jank. Entire sections of wall can be removed by a missed pistol shot, leaving you exposed to instant death from a flanking attack. Overwatch sometimes just doesn't work. Getting wiped because my sniper refused to take a pistol overwatch shot against a 1 health chrysallid coming around the corner is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. I put them there to handle that exact thing from happening. The glitches and jank decided my strategizing meant nothing. If you're playing EW, be aware that throwing a battle scanner and revealing a pod of seekers before activating them with your troops will result in a softlock. The ability I explicitly took to deal with seekers actually just makes the game literally unplayable. INCREDIBLE. Nothing I do matters because the game is a janky, glitch filled mess and no amount of risk management or strategizing or positioning will ever fix that.

And then there's the freezing. If I let the game finish the cutscene for the skyranger landing back at base, the game freezes my computer. I have verified file integrity, uninstalled and reinstalled the game, updated my drivers, and every other thing I could think of and it still happens.

Overall, wh…

cohorts.label: 100h+
cohorts.summary: Veteran players navigate intense tactical combat driven entirely by unpredictable probability swings.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the tactical combat as heavily influenced by random number generation, leading to frustrating misses on high-percentage shots or surprising hits on low-percentage shots.

citations.review_text: Honestly I've had so much fun with this game. "That's X-Com baby!" absolutely defines some of the RNG madness that can happen in this game, such as getting an impossible kill with 15% chance to hit or having your best trooper miss with a 95% chance to hit while standing right next to the target with a shotgun. The tactical strategy behind X-Com: Enemy Unknown is really cunning as at the start of the game you're fully on the back foot with your weapon and technology level against the invaders, only to slowly claw your way up to parity with every bloody victory you pull off. Getting all the DLCs is completely worth it as it added story to the game that distantly ties it in with The Bureau: XCOM Declassified along with a whole pile of new challenges. Can't recommend this game enough if you love turn-based strategy games. Movies are excellent, music is excellent, depth behind your team is great as you really love "your crew" as they hold back the tied of death and it's just an all-round diamond package.

This game used to be a perfect turn based game. But  lately the game is broken.  When i purchase something trough engineering it will randomly take more money then it should have(some times a lot more).  The next thing is the hit percentage is broken. When i have enemies close the alien skull will read a very low hit chance but when i go to attack it will show a higher percent. The issue is 80% of the time it will hit at the alien skull low percent. Sad this is a great game but these issues are game breakers.

Steam really needs to add some kind of a "Mixed" to reviews. XCOM Enemy Within is a suberp tactical turn based strategy game. The playtime I hit without even realising it, the game continues to keep me coming back but there are countless times classic ironman runs I've failed due to missed shots I damn well know should've landed, but because of "RNG"? It says f*** you and I can hear that annoying meme "that's xcom baby" creeping in. 

If you enjoy torture, love turn based games, get addicted easily and are stubborn like me? XCOM is for you. Now excuse me, I'm going to start a fresh Classic Ironman run until I beat this damn game. P.s. F*** Thin Men, Sectapods and Chrysalids.
